claims.text: A CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy coating can adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix.
Interface modification by a CrMnFeCoNi coating enhances interfacial bonding and adhesion to Cu.
The initial substrate is a pure Cu matrix.
The CrMnFeCoNi coating is deposited by a technique such as magnetron sputtering.
The coating thickness is approximately 5 micrometers.
Deposition is performed under vacuum at a substrate temperature of 200°C.
Deposition forms a thin interfacial layer containing a mixture of Cu and HEA elements.
The mixed interfacial layer facilitates a strong bond between the Cu matrix and the HEA coating.
Interdiffusion of elements across the coating–substrate interface produces a strong metallurgical bond.
Intermetallic compounds may form at the interface.
Interfacial intermetallic compounds would further strengthen the coating–substrate interface.
The HEA coating increases adhesion strength by at least 30% relative to a pure Cu coating on Cu.
The predicted adhesion increase is measured by scratch testing at a load of 10 N.
The expected adhesion-strength increase lies between 25% and 40%.
Deposition conditions, substrate roughness, oxidation, and contamination can cause variation in adhesion strength.
An adhesion increase below 20% relative to the pure-Cu-coated control falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome states an increase of at least 30%, whereas the stated expected range begins at 25%; outcomes from 25% to below 30% satisfy the boundary but contradict the stated minimum.
